items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Gesler Gunther seeing 'the Chocolate-teers' and liking 'his impressions'. The interviewee refers to 'he' (Mosley/Chuckles) but does not claim a personal relationship with Gesler Gunther, only that she was involved in the professional discovery of the interviewe

ctx.x: So, like they used to demonstrate these tournaments. They acquired themselves a better -- a greater brotherly love, I would call it. And they was always hoping that someday maneuvers would arrive and gather them all together in some kind of mania. And fortunately, it happened to happen to me, you see. And I was talking about -- thinking about how could I do -- what would I do without Chuckles, you see, because Chuckles was -- he was back in the business. But he had got in the situation that I was in in the…

So, he took some fellow's place named Mosley. He used to be in the Three Chocolate-teers. And, well, he got rediscovered. Some woman imported a fraulein over in the fatherland, father-land, and they called her Gesler Gunther, you know. And she happened to see him, or some of her managers or somebody saw the Chocolate-teers over there with -- I think it was something about the Joy Train or something. Duke Ellington, you know.

And she liked the way he was -- his impressions, you know. He was so impressive, you see, because he's tall and he really was what they call -- I call a true slim, you know, because I mean he's -- I couldn't blame the lady, you know. She's fortunate, you see. You see, I thought I was lucky enough to have a friend like that as a child, you see, and to grow up with. But, I mean, you know so much for -- but he became like Jimmy Chuckles Walker, see. He got a chance to use his whole family name, you see.
